text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- President Arpad Goncz on Monday appointed the youngest son of Otto Habsburg, Gyorgy Habsburg, as ambassador extraordinary and plenipotentiary to promote the nation's interests within the EU. @
- Parliament will hold the final vote tomorrow on a 1997 budget that projects a deficit of HUF 309.7 billion, HUF 8 billion more than originally planned.

- Parliament's Monday session saw the latest flare-up of debate concerning a decision to place an 80-year stamp of secrecy on data concerning the "oilgate" affair, with the Free Democrats asking the government ombudsman to review the decision.
- Tamas Isepy, parliamentary caucus chief of the Christian Democrats confirmed that despite a weekend call to resign from his post, he has no plans to do so. @
- Romanian MPs are to attend the next pan-Hungarian summit, in early 1997, the head of the World Federation of Hungarians said.

- The economic cabinet proposes that the $1,750 upper limit of the annual foreign exchange purchase for travel purposes be abolished from January, announced Finance Ministry State Secretary Tibor Draskovics.

- The East European Food Fund owned by British pension funds and investment banks and registered in Luxembourg, is to raise the registered capital of coop company Csopak Szovetkezeti Rt. to HUF 2.2 billion from HUF 1.5 billion. @
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze signed an extradition treaty with his French counterpart, Jean-Louis Debre, in Paris.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs met his Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen in Beijing yesterday.
NEPSZABADSAG

- At the end of the year, the total figure of registered unemployed is estimated to be 480,000, or 10-11 percent of the population able to work, the same as last year, according to Gyorgy Lazar of the National Labour Office.
NAPI GAZDASAG @
- According to 1997 central budget bill to be approved by Parliament this week, the State Privatisation and Holding Co. will pay a total of HUF 72 billion into the central budget next year.
- Fotex group CEO Gabor Varszegi projects much higher sales for the fourth quarter than in the same period of last year, but lower profits for 1996 as a whole.
- Unicbank Rt. shareholders raised the bank's HUF 4.356 billion registered capital to HUF 7 billion at the AGM yesterday. @

- The economic cabinet has decided to propose to the government that companies having a stake in electricity distribution companies be able to sell their stakes within five years from the time of purchase.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- The OECD considers the achievements of the economic progress of Hungary favourable and finds we have again become the leading reform country in the region," said Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy following his participation at the "Forum for the Future" conference held in Paris. @
- Sony electronics company representatives said that Sony's ultimate goal is to use only Hungarian-made components for the products at its plant in Godollo.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
